result.summary: Repaired both files against the flagged gaps, no production edits. `equipment_authority_lifetime_focus.gd` is now `extends "res://test/run_tests.gd"` and only overrides `_discover_suites()` to return exactly the five required suite paths in the stated order; it inherits the base runner's worker/supervisor protocol verbatim, so there is no standalone/undiscovered witness path anymore — running it exercises the real worker/supervisor pass/fail machinery restricted to those five files. The two real Gear/Inventory/Residents lifecycle scenarios (`_mutual_release_without_unbind`, `_gear_alone_retains_its_collaborators`) were moved out of that file and into `test_equipment_authority_lifetime.gd` as `test_real_gear_inventory_residents_mutually_release_without_unbind` and `test_real_gear_alone_retains_inventory_and_residents_until_gear_is_dropped`, built from a new `_bind_real_triple()` helper using the exact production `InventoryScript.new()` / `ResidentsScript.new()` / `GearScript.new()` / `bind_equipment()` calls the shutdown probe uses, with weakrefs checked at both the intermediate (Gear-alone-alive) and final (all-released) points; `_bind_real_triple()` returns an empty Dictionary on a genuine bind refusal and both new tests return immediately rather than call `weakref()` on a null object or draw a false conclusion from a failed setup. Added `test_binding_refuses_while_a_transaction_is_open_and_preserves_the_prior_authority`, which opens a real explicit transaction, gets `REFUSE_TRANSACTION_OPEN` (the existing code) for both a replacement bind and a null unbind with `state_bytes()` unchanged, then `abort()`s and shows the original authority still attests for the same lot while the candidate authority is never consulted for it. `_assert_four_gates_refuse_invalid` now asserts `assert_false(op.ok, ...)` alongside the exact error and the unchanged full `state_bytes()` for each of the four gates. Added a `_stopped(ref)` guard and threaded it through every existing and new scenario that chains `_container()`/`_tool_lot()`/`_equip()` results, so a refused fixture handle now stops that scenario (`return`) instead of being used as if it were real, and `_equip()` itself never returns a ref for a create or detach that actually refused. The Node four-gate test and the self-dropping-authority per-call test now call `.free()` / clear the holder array on every exit path, including early-stop, so the Node frees exactly once and no transient holder/authority cycle is left unbroken. All eleven previously-accepted tests remain, unchanged in what they assert, only hardened with the stop guard; no production file or existing passing behavior was altered. I have not executed either file; this reports only what the diff does.

extends "res://test/run_tests.gd"
## Focused runner for EQUIPMENT-LIFETIME-R01v1 (ADR 0187).
##
## Inherits `test/run_tests.gd`'s exact worker/supervisor protocol -- the same process split,
## the same script-error auditing, the same pass/fail accounting -- and overrides only which
## suites are discovered, so nothing here is a standalone or hidden witness: every scenario
## this review needs runs through the real discovered-suite path. Usage is identical to the
## full runner:
##     godot --headless --path godot --script test/equipment_authority_lifetime_focus.gd

const FOCUS_SUITES: PackedStringArray = PackedStringArray([
	"res://test/test_equipment_authority_lifetime.gd",
	"res://test/test_inventory.gd",
	"res://test/test_gear.gd",
	"res://test/test_stock_authority_lifetime.gd",
	"res://test/test_settlement_system.gd",
])


func _discover_suites() -> PackedStringArray:
	"""Override discovery: exactly the five suites this review requires, in the stated order."""
	return FOCUS_SUITES
